subject.title: fix(logging): boot credentials lose exact-value redaction after transient secret churn

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this separate 512-entry durable redaction tier for audit identity keys and SecretRef-resolved runtime values, accepting up to 1,024 retained exact forms and eviction-only retirement of rotated values?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically coherent, but the durable caller set, combined memory/redaction budget, and retirement semantics define the product's credential-handling security boundary rather than a purely local bug fix.

options.title: Approve the bounded durable tier
options.body: Accept the proposed audit-key and SecretRef caller set, with separate 512-entry durable and transient budgets, then merge after normal final checks.

options.title: Require lifecycle-scoped retirement
options.body: Keep the fix direction but revise the durable store to retire values when their config or auth owner is replaced, reducing stale over-redaction.

options.title: Choose a narrower durable caller set
options.body: Keep the tier but permit only explicitly named boot credentials until broader SecretRef lifecycle ownership is designed.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded durable tier
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed audit-key and SecretRef caller set, with separate 512-entry durable and transient budgets, then merge after normal final checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR identifies this security code-owner route for the affected SecretRef boundary and asks it to decide the retention policy.
